result.summary: Aro is a C compiler/frontend written in Zig. This surface is its build.zig, its build.zig.zon and its bundled standard C headers. The build script defines modules, runs a local generator over builtin .def tables, installs the headers and defines optional test, fuzz and Tracy steps; it has no network access, no hidden commands and no encoded payloads. The headers are plain macro and typedef definitions.

findings.title: Build-time code generation from .def files
findings.detail: build.zig compiles build/generate_def.zig for the host and runs it on the Builtins/*.def files in src/aro to produce Zig modules. This is ordinary table generation for compiler builtins. The generator's own source is not part of this surface; what it does is consistent with its name and inputs.

findings.title: Unreachable git invocation and opt-in system commands
findings.detail: A `git describe` invocation sits behind `if (true) break :v version_string;`, so it never runs. The fuzz step's afl-clang-lto command, the tests and the Tracy integration only run when the user explicitly asks for those steps or options.

findings.title: Bundled C headers are standard definitions
findings.detail: The include/*.h files are standard freestanding C headers: limits, stdint, stdatomic, stdarg and similar. They contain only macros and typedefs mapped to compiler builtins. There is no executable payload.
